sections.h2: Ways to sell in West Bend
sections.html:
West Bend owners can hire an agent, sell alone, or accept a cash buyer's offer. At the finish, every one of them needs a deed on record with Washington County and a transfer return filed with the state.

The house's condition and your calendar settle the choice.

  • With an agent, a house in good repair sells best, provided you can wait out showings, an inspection and the buyer's loan.
  • Going alone saves the agent's fee, though pricing, paperwork and negotiating land on you.
  • A cash offer is for a house that needs work, a West Bend property you inherited, or a sale where timing outranks the last dollar.

Put each offer's terms on paper and compare the net after the transfer fee, taxes owed and repairs.

West Bend is the Washington County seat, in the Milwaukee metropolitan area, with an estimated 32,268 residents in 2025, up from 31,752 at the 2020 census. Homes are valued below the county median, and a higher share of households rent. A lot of houses went up during the postwar growth, which is why buyers focus on the roof, furnace and basement.

These are medians for the whole city, so a particular street can sit well above or below them.

Cold, snowy winters put the heating system and roof at the top of a buyer's list. West Bend sits in the Kettle Moraine region, where glaciers left kettles and hills, and hilly ground can send runoff toward a foundation. Keep a note of any grading or drainage work. Storm damage history is also a normal question from buyers.

Before you list, gather paperwork for these items:

  • Roof, siding and window replacement dates, with the City permit if one was pulled.
  • Furnace and air conditioner age and service records.
  • Any basement water repair, sump pump work or insurance claim.

Buyers ask about the West Bend School District and the route to Milwaukee. West Bend East and West High Schools will consolidate into a single West Bend High School for the 2027-2028 school year. For commuting, US 45 runs as a freeway bypass west of downtown, with Wisconsin 33 and Wisconsin 144 also serving the city. The Washington County Commuter Express bus to Milwaukee ended in 2023, so most commuters drive, and the average trip to work is 25.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Which City of West Bend permits matter before you sell?
sections.html:
Work done without a permit can slow a sale, so check your permit history with the City of West Bend Building Inspection office at (262) 335-5140. Permits must be obtained before any building activity begins, and inspections are scheduled within 24 to 48 hours of a request.

A permit is required for each of these:

  • Finishing a basement, remodeling living space, adding a dormer, an addition or a three-season room.
  • Adding or replacing a deck or porch.
  • Replacing roofing or siding.
  • Installing a shed, fence, driveway or swimming pool.
  • Replacing a furnace or air conditioner.

Detached garages and other accessory structures are capped at 720 square feet in total, and a detached garage at 18 feet in height. The owner and occupant of a single-family home may do their own electrical and plumbing work with a permit. Duplex and condo owners may not, and no homeowner may work on the electrical service to the home or on a pool or spa. Suspect a previous owner skipped a permit? Ask the office how to close it out before the buyer's inspector turns it up.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Washington County
sections.html:
A standard document costs $30 to record, a figure that comes from Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag). On top of that, the seller owes the state 30 cents on each $100 of value, or $3 per $1,000, under Wis. Stat. 77.22(1).

The register takes the fee as the deed arrives. Before that, a transfer return has to be filed online with the Department of Revenue, and its receipt travels with the deed. Call 262-335-4320 to reach the Washington County Register of Deeds.

A few transfers owe nothing under Wis. Stat. 77.25. Homeowners most often meet these: inheritance transfers, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, gifts within a family line for little or no payment, and any transfer of real estate worth $1,000 or less.

One more local tool is LandNotification, a free email alert. Pick a name or a parcel, and you hear when a document is recorded against it. A recording alone does not move ownership, so the alert helps you catch a bogus filing early.

sections.h2: Property taxes when a West Bend house sells
sections.html:
West Bend property tax is billed in arrears, so buyer and seller usually prorate it at closing. Bills are out by the third Monday in December. Under Wis. Stat. 74.11 the tax splits into two equal installments, one due January 31 and one July 31. A bill under $100 is due whole by January 31.

Watch the first deadline. If that installment is not received within five working days after January 31, the entire unpaid balance turns delinquent as of February 1. Anyone who is behind should call the Washington County treasurer for the exact balance, interest included, and let the title company pay it from the sale proceeds.

Owners living in the house may see the lottery and gaming credit on the bill. It stays with the property at sale, so it belongs in the proration. A buyer who will live there files a fresh application.

Buyers in West Bend usually ask for permit history, service records and any record of water in the basement. Store them in a single folder before showing day. If you handled electrical or plumbing work yourself, make sure the permit was pulled, since the city allows owner work only with one.

Include your vesting deed and a recent tax bill. Once offers arrive, ask every buyer for a closing date, a statement of who pays title and recording, and a yes or no on a loan. A cash buyer purchases as-is, which can remove the repair list, but the written terms still matter.

faqs.q: How is the transfer fee figured on a West Bend sale?
faqs.a: Multiply the sale price by 0.30 percent. Take the price in hundreds and charge 30 cents each, counting a leftover fraction as a full hundred. The register takes payment with the deed.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee in West Bend?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. Wis. Stat. 77.22(1) names the grantor as the payer, and Washington County's register collects it on recording.

faqs.q: Can I do my own electrical or plumbing work on my West Bend house?
faqs.a: Yes, if you live in your single-family home, and the permit still has to be pulled. Duplex and condo owners may not do their own work, and no homeowner may touch the electrical service or work on a swimming pool or spa.

faqs.q: Does the lottery credit go to the buyer of my West Bend house?
faqs.a: It remains with the property and comes off the next bill, so include it when prorating. The buyer files a new application if moving in.

faqs.q: How can I watch for deed fraud on my West Bend property?
faqs.a: Sign up for the county's LandNotification email alert on your name or parcel. A recording does not automatically change ownership. If you suspect fraud, tell the police and your title insurer.
